field_notes.record_type: Name the dangling record type: CNAME, NS, MX, SPF/TXT include, or apex/registration-level.
field_notes.cname_chain: List the full resolution chain observed (host -> CNAME target -> further CNAME/A, or NXDOMAIN at which hop), each hop resolved via a named public resolver.
field_notes.provider_classification: Name the suspected provider/service the dangling target belongs to (S3, Azure App Service, GitHub Pages, ELB/ALB, etc.) and the fingerprint that identified it, or unknown.
field_notes.claimability: One of: claimable (name/resource is attacker-choosable and unclaimed), non_claimable (provider assigns a random/non-choosable suffix), unverified (provider claimability not yet checked), or already_claimed_by_third_party.
field_notes.false_positive_controls: State whether wildcard DNS or domain-wide parking was ruled out, and how (e.g. a made-up sibling hostname tested against a public resolver).
field_notes.required_evidence: What's still needed to move from hypothesis to confirmed: e.g. a name-availability check result, a second public resolver confirmation, a WHOIS/registration-expiry check.
field_notes.safe_next_step: One bounded next step, preferring a no-resource-created verification (name-availability check, second resolver confirmation) over an actual claim unless manual approval already exists.
field_notes.manual_gate_required: true for any step in safety.md's Manual-Gated Lane: actually claiming a resource, deploying content, reading real visitor data, or touching an NS/MX dangling record.
